messages.content: Hi there, it’s really nice to meet you. How have you been feeling lately, in general? And what kinds of things have you found yourself enjoying, or looking forward to, recently?

I've been okay, I guess. Just a bit... tired. I work part-time and then help my parents with their grocery shopping, so it’s a lot. But honestly, I don’t know if I can say I’m looking forward to anything specific right now.

That sounds like a lot to manage, and I appreciate you telling me. Have you been feeling sad lately, and have you noticed any changes in your sleep—like trouble getting to sleep, waking up during the night, or feeling less rested in the morning?
Yeah, I wake up a lot. Sometimes I lie there for hours, thinking about how I’m not really doing what I want to do with my life. It’s hard to explain, but it feels like I’m just drifting along.
That sounds really rough to deal with, and I appreciate you telling me about it. Have you been finding it harder to decide things lately or to concentrate on tasks?

Yeah, I get stuck on the smallest things. I'll be trying to pick out a book, and I'll stare at the shelves for 20 minutes because I can't decide. It’s frustrating, but I just can’t seem to focus right now.
That sounds like a lot to carry, and I really appreciate you sharing this with me. Have you been feeling sad or low lately, and have you noticed any changes in your appetite or eating habits?
I eat, but I don't really taste it. It’s like my body is just going through the motions, you know?

That sounds really heavy to carry, and I appreciate you sharing. Have you been feeling sad lately, and when those feelings show up, do you find yourself being hard on yourself or feeling guilty about what you should have done differently?
Yeah, I beat myself up about it. I think about how I should be doing better, but I just can’t seem to get my head straight.
That sounds really heavy to carry, and I appreciate you sharing how you're feeling. Have you been feeling sad lately, and if so, how often does that come up for you?
It comes up a lot, honestly. I try to distract myself with TV or my phone, but it’s always there in the background.

That sounds heavy to carry, and I appreciate you sharing that. When thoughts like “I’m not good enough” or “I should be doing more” pop up, how often do they show up and how long do they tend to last? If those moments come with crying or feeling restless, what usually seems to trigger them or make them worse?
They come up a lot. They usually last a few hours, and then I just go back to work or errands. I don't know if I can explain it, but it feels like the sadness just sort of... settles in.

That sounds heavy to carry, and I really appreciate you sharing. When those moments come up, do you end up crying, feeling agitated or irritable, or sensing that you’re not worth much? How often do these feelings show up and how long do they last, and do they tend to happen in certain situations?
Yeah, I usually cry. It usually lasts a few hours, then I just get tired and go to bed. It happens when I’m alone, mostly.

That sounds like a heavy load to carry, and I really appreciate you sharing how much you’ve been juggling. Have you been feeling more on edge or irritable lately, like you can’t sit still or you snap at small things, and in those moments do you also catch yourself thinking you’re not doing enough or that you’re not worth the effort?
Yeah, I snap. And yeah, I think it. It’s just... I don't know how to stop it, so I just sit there and feel like I’m wasting everyone's time.

That sounds really heavy, and I appreciate you sharing how much you’re carrying. When those thoughts creep in that you’re not worth much or that you should be doing more, how often do they show up and how long do they tend to last?
They come up every day. They usually last a few hours, but sometimes they go on for days.

That sounds heavy, and I really appreciate you sharing. When those self-judging thoughts pop up—like "I'm not good enough" or "I should be doing more"—how often do they come, and how long do they tend to last? Do they show up more when you’re alone or in specific situations like at work or with your parents?
They come up every day, usually in the afternoon or evening. They last a few hours, and they happen mostly when I’m alone.

That sounds really rough to deal with. You mentioned snapping at small things and feeling on edge—how often does irritability show up, and does it tend to happen in specific situations (like at work or with your parents) or at certain times of day?
It happens a lot. Mostly in the afternoon or evening when I’m tired.

That sounds really heavy, and I really appreciate you sharing how you’re feeling. When those thoughts that you’re not worth much or that you should be doing more pop up, how much do they affect your day or the things you try to do?
A lot. They make it hard to focus or make decisions.

That sounds really heavy to carry. You mentioned these self-critical thoughts come up every day, usually in the afternoon or evening, and they last a few hours, especially when you're alone. what tends to make them feel most intense, and how do they affect what you’re trying to do in those moments?
It’s usually when I’m lying in bed. I just lie there and think about how I’m failing everyone.

Thank you so much for being open and for sharing what you’ve been going through today. I really appreciate your honesty and the effort you’ve put into our chat. I hope you have a calmer, gentler day ahead and take care.
